sections.title: Evergreen oak
sections.text: The holm oak is an evergreen tree or shrub native from southern-central Europe around the Mediterranean. It can reach about 25 m, exceptionally 30 m; its crown may become broad, and the leathery leaves are glossy dark green above and pale beneath.

sections.title: Flowers and acorns
sections.text: Yellowish male catkins and small female flowers appear in spring. The acorns mature in their first year and are usually about 1.5–2 cm long. Although acorns are eaten in some traditional livestock systems, their suitability for people depends on type and preparation; safe preparation was not established by the sources consulted.

sections.title: Comparison
sections.text: Unlike the deciduous downy oak and northern red oak, Q. ilex keeps its leaves through the year. Its unlobed, holly-like leaves distinguish it from both.
